newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy minister meets transport firms over strikes.
newsitem.headline: Italy minister meets transport firms over strikes.

text.p: Transport Minister Claudio Burlando met transport companies on Wednesday to try to avert a string of strikes over contract disputes, which threaten to paralayse Italy over the next two weeks.
Air traffic controllers called off a planned strike on Wednesday in a brief respite from the stoppages but bus, tram and metro drivers were expected to go ahead with industrial action on Thursday.

Air traffic control unions in Milan have announced a one-day stoppage on April 18 and a four-day sea transport strike was due to start on April 19. Railway workers have called a 24-hour walkout for the same day.
A four-day strike by petrol pump attendants, unhappy with moves to reorganise the sector, is planned to start next Monday.

A wildcat bus drivers' strike in Rome on Tuesday brought chaos to the capital as commuters struggled to reach work. Public transport workers in the region want the government to renew work contracts which expired over 15 months ago.
The mayor of Rome, Francesco Rutelli, has asked for those responsible for the impromptu action to be sacked.

Burlando said he hoped dialogue with the unions would prevail. "We are working to change what was a truce into a long-term agreement on a plan to change the Italian transport system, which is at the moment far behind other countries."
